Testimony of Francine Garland Stark In Support of (Amended) LD 1598: "An Act to Provide Relocation Assistance to Victims of
Domestic Violence, Sexual Assault and Sex Trafficking" Thursday, April 17, 2025
Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, and members of the Joint Standing Committee
on Judiciary, I am Francine Garland Stark, Executive Director, speaking on behalf of the
Maine Coalition to End Domestic Violence (MCEDV)` to offer our support for Representative Stover's proposed amendment to LD 1598, An Act to Provide Relocation Assistance to
Victims of Domestic Violence, Sexual Assault and Sex Trafficking.
The intent of this bill is incredibly responsive to the needs of survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and sex trafficking. Victims of these crimes often need to consider and take steps to relocate for safety, for stability, and for peace of mind. Maine's victim services providers collaborate very closely with Maine's Victim Compensation Fund Program, a program operated through the Maine Office of the Attorney General. Rules promulgated by the Victim Compensation Fund Board already partly address needs of these victims for financial support for relocation. Because the VCF's application processing takes some time, time that is not often able to accommodate the immediate needs of these victims for relocation support, the VCF program has a long history of collaboration with victim services
providers. This collaboration involves local victim services providers granting a victim with
financial assistance to support some relocation expenses, specifically a security deposit on a new apartment, up front. The VCF then arranges with the local victim services provider to
reimburse those costs.
Much of the language in the original bill draft would work to create procedural and
substantive barriers to the current process for supporting victims with relocation that has
been established collaboratively between victim services providers and the VCF program. Understanding Representative Stover's longstanding commitment to advocacy for effective
solutions to identified needs of crime victims, MCEDV has worked with Representative
Stover to bring forward an enhancement to the Victim Compensation Fund's authorizing statute that would move the ball forward in terms of the VCF's ability to respond more
comprehensively to a crime victim's relocation needs.

Though this amendment changes only a few words in the statute, it will lead to rulemaking that will allow the VCF to expand the types of relocation costs it can reimburse for, which will deepen the community collaboration and allow it to respond more comprehensively to sun/ivor needs. This change would allow the VCF to potentially reimburse for things like a moving van, a few nights in a hotel while transitioning from one home to another, and things like plane or bus tickets when safety and stability necessitate
long-distance relocation.
The slight change proposed in Representative Stover's amendment will have a
measurable impact. We encourage you to support it.

Testimony of Representative Holly B. Stover presenting
LD 1598, An Act to Provide Relocation Assistance to Victims of
Domestic Violence, Sexual Assault and Sex Trafficking
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Judiciary

Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Judiciary, my name is Holly Stover, and I am here today to present LD 1598, An Act to Provide
Relocation Assistance to Victims of Domestic Violence, Sexual Assault and Sex Trafficking.

Domestic violence and sexual assault happen in every one of our communities. Each year, Maine's domestic violence prevention and response programs work with thousands of people
from every corner of our state who are experiencing violence and abuse. Roughly half of them have at least one child in their home. Many of these individuals need help finding and securing a
safe, stable place to live for themselves -- and often for their children as well.

During my career, which has included time as director of the Office of Violence Prevention within the Maine Department of Health and Human Services and as a member of the Domestic
Abuse Homicide Review Panel, I have seen time and time again how critically important it is to
provide survivors with direct support so that they can escape violence, keep themselves and their families safe, and begin to rebuild their lives.
Too often, this is literally a matter of life and death. We know that nearly half of all homicides in
Maine are the result of domestic violence. When it comes to our response, the stakes could not
be higher.
LD 1598 seeks to expand the support and resources available to survivors. Since submitting the
bill, I have Worked with stakeholders to propose an amendment to the bill as drafted, which is attached to this testimony and I believe will better achieve its goal. As drafted, the bill could unintentionally limit assistance to survivors, particularly those who are victimized more than once, and slow down the process of getting suppolt to those who need it most urgently. Instead,

survivors.
All people deserve a life free from violence, coercion and fear. Please support LD 1598 as we are
proposing to amend it. Thank you for your consideration. I would be happy to answer any questions you have for me.

Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Judiciary:
My name is Melissa Martin, and I am offering testimony today on behalf of the Maine Coalition Against Sexual Assault (MECASA), the organization which represents and serves Maine's sexual violence prevention and response programs as well as Maine's Children's Advocacy Centers. MECASA initiates and advocates for victim-centered public policy; provides expert training, technical assistance, and resources for providers and partners; and funds the service providers in your communities.
MECASA is here today in support of LD 1598 as amended, "An Act to Provide Relocation Assistance to Victims of Domestic Violence, Sexual Assault and Sex Trafficking." Thank you to Representative Stover for sponsoring this important legislation.
Sexual violence is a serious and costly public health problem in the Maine--nearly one in five adult Maine residents reports that they have been the victim of rape or attempted rape during their lifetime.1 Roughly 14,000 Maine residents may be the victim of rape or unwanted sexual activity during any 12 month period.2 Sexual assault results in more than $122,000 in costs per victim.3 With about 25 million rape survivors in the U.S. right now, we can expect to spend more than $3 trillion over their lifetimes on health care, criminal justice response, lost productivity, and other costs.4

One of the costs that sexual violence survivors face is the cost of relocation after sexual harm has occurred. Survivors may want or need to relocate for a variety of reasons, including but not limited to concerns for their physical safety and the traumatic impact of remaining in the home or community where the violence occurred.5 Therefore, it is essential that the victim's compensation fund in Maine be able to provide for these costs.
Reimbursing relocation costs can help Maine create better support systems for survivors of interpersonal violence while also being a smart investment that saves money in the long run. When survivors can move safely to a new place, they are less likely to experience violence again and can avoid ongoing psychological damage, resulting in a decreased need for mental health support, emergency services, and legal aid. Survivors who settle in safe environments are more likely to find employment and contribute to the economy compared to those who continue to struggle with the effects of trauma.6 Therefore, providing help for relocation is a proactive way to ease systemic strain and build stronger, more resilient communities.
For these reasons, we strongly support the bill as amended. Thank you for your consideration. We hope you will support LD 1598 as amended.
About Maine's Sexual Assault Service Providers
One in five Mainers will experience sexual assault at some point in their lifetime.7 Each year, 19,000 Mainers will experience sexual violence.8
Maine's sexual violence service providers provide free and confidential services across the state to victims/survivors of sexual harassment and sexual assault and those close to them, as well as to individuals who wish to increase their understanding of the issues. Just some of the services include a 24-hour statewide sexual assault helpline, crisis intervention and information, support
